n: Synthetic and AI-Generated Identity and Deepfake Onboarding
ds: Fraudsters combine real and fabricated data, or use generative tools to create faces, voices and documents, to pass remote onboarding. The accounts then bear credit abuse, mule activity or laundering. Detection depends on layered identity proofing and behavioural signals across the customer lifecycle.

src.t: FinCEN, Alert on Fraud Schemes Involving Deepfake Media Targeting Financial Institutions (FIN-2024-Alert004, 2024)

cn.rt: Synthetic and deepfake identities in remote applications drive bust-out, loan fraud and mule use; voice cloning hits phone banking.

rat: Synthetic/deepfake identities in remote onboarding leading to credit bust-out and mule use.

ind.n: Identity with thin or recently created credit and data footprint
ind.cx: Identifiers appear in few databases, with recent first use and mixed data elements.
ind.ds: Thin or recently created credit and digital footprint, with mixed attributes suggesting a fabricated identity.
ind.cn: Synthetic identity with thin or newly created footprint

ind.n: Selfie or video shows signs of synthetic or injected media
ind.cx: Liveness checks reveal artefacts, virtual cameras or replayed streams.
ind.ds: Liveness checks reveal artefacts, virtual cameras or replayed streams.

ind.n: Document images share templates, fonts or backgrounds across applicants
ind.cx: Multiple applications use near-identical layouts or reused photos.
ind.ds: Same document image, selfie, template, font or background appears across different applicants or after rejection.
ind.cn: Documents or images reused or templated across applicants

ind.n: Mismatch between claimed identity and device, IP or voice
ind.cx: Geolocation, language or voice biometrics inconsistent with the stated identity.
ind.ds: Geolocation, language or voice biometrics inconsistent with the stated identity.

ind.n: Same contact details used with different identities
ind.cx: Phone or email repeated under varied names or birthdates. Many identities share one address or commercial drop.
ind.ds: Unrelated customers or applicants share the same phone, email, address, device or bank account, including mail drops and shared accommodation.
ind.cn: Multiple customers sharing contact details or addresses

ind.n: Rapid credit build then bust or large cash-out
ind.cx: Account builds limits quickly then draws maximum funds.
ind.ds: Credit builds up and is then rapidly utilised to limit or cashed out after a period of low use.
ind.cn: Sudden credit utilisation spike then bust-out

ind.n: Voice or video call authentication challenges failed
ind.cx: Callers using cloned voices or video deepfakes during high-value requests.
ind.ds: Callers using cloned voices or video deepfakes during high-value requests.

ind.n: Applications following failed attempts with edited data
ind.cx: Repeated retries altering one data element until approval.
ind.ds: Repeated retries altering one data element until approval.

ind.n: Dates of birth, SSN or national ID not matching authoritative records
ind.cx: Authoritative checks fail or show multiple identities on one number.
ind.ds: Authoritative checks fail or show multiple identities on one number.

ctl.n: Duplicate and synthetic identity checks at onboarding
ctl.ds: Compares new applicant identifiers such as name, email, phone, address, device and bank account with existing customers, previously declined or exited applicants and known-bad data. Matches are blocked or referred, limiting repeat applicants, synthetic identities and mule recruitment.

Checks identity and supporting documents for tampering, forgery, template reuse and internal inconsistency, and corroborates their data against authoritative or reliable independent sources. It exposes altered or counterfeit credentials that pass a visual check.
Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.

Remote verification of a person's identity using document capture, biometric matching and liveness or anti-spoofing checks, or a trusted digital identity. It reduces impersonation, synthetic identities and account opening with stolen or fabricated credentials.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.

Detects use of VPN, proxy and anonymising services and compares access geolocation with declared residence and sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions. It reveals concealed location and supports geographic restrictions.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

ctl.n: Specialist investigation and suspicious activity reporting
ctl.ds: Trained analysts investigate alerts with typology playbooks, document rationale and file reports where suspicion is formed, with prompt reporting to the competent authority. It converts alerts into actionable intelligence.
Requires phishing-resistant authentication and additional verification on risky sessions, credential or payee changes and large payments. It blocks unauthorised access and payments.
